top_signals.title: Hormuz Tanker Traffic Slumps as Saudi Arabia Scrambles for New Oil Routes
top_signals.summary: Only four commodity vessels were detected to have moved inbound or out of the Strait of Hormuz on Thursday, shipping data showed early on Friday, while oil shipping options out of the Middle East became fewer with the closure of the Saudi pipeline to the Red Sea port of Yanbu. Three vessels moved into the Persian Gulf, and one exited the Strait on Thursday, down from the 10-day average of as many as 16 ships daily transiting the chokepoint, according to preliminary data from Kpler cited by Reuters. The tracking excludes any movements of ships that…
top_signals.why_it_matters: Geopolitical escalation affecting commodities, shipping and cross-asset volatility.

top_signals.title: Bank of Japan raises interest rates to 31-year high, flags concerns over inflation
top_signals.summary: The decision was split 7-2, with board members Toichiro Asada and Ayano Sato dissenting from the hike.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Central-bank repricing affecting yields, FX, liquidity and equities.

top_signals.title: Bill to curb AI data center utility costs hits snag in Senate
top_signals.summary: Sen. Martin Heinrich, D-N.M., blocked bipartisan legislation aimed at reining in data center-related utility cost increases, calling the bill a half-measure.
top_signals.why_it_matters: AI and semiconductor developments impacting technology leadership and capex cycles.

top_signals.title: Helios, Mavericks’ Ujiri Back $294 Million Sports Arena in Kenya
top_signals.summary: Zaria Group, a firm backed by Dallas Mavericks President Masai Ujiri and Helios Sports & Entertainment Group, plans to build a 10,000-seater multipurpose indoor arena in the Kenyan capital Nairobi, according to regulatory filings.
